key_insight: Reliable neural hyperelastic calibration depends less on the neural architecture alone and more on rich, well-resolved full-field deformation data that spans the right deformation modes.
engineering_relevance: For full-field solid mechanics testing, specimen design, measurement resolution, and load-path coverage directly determine whether a learned constitutive model will generalize to new geometries and loading cases.
method: Studied equilibrium gap-based calibration of isotropic, polyconvex hyperelastic physics-augmented neural networks (PANNs).
Tested sensitivity to under-resolved surface displacement fields and non-negligible specimen thickness using synthetic data.
Validated on real experiments with multiple inhomogeneous specimen geometries to assess generalization across unseen cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports synthetic and real-data evaluations showing that calibration performance and extrapolation depend strongly on deformation-state coverage, especially the presence of biaxial-tension-like states.
watch_item: Models using the second deformation invariant can extrapolate unphysically toward equi-biaxial tension if calibration data do not include sufficiently biaxial loading states.
paper_title: Reliable training of neural hyperelastic models via full-field data
